stem:
In a grass field Kabir studies, the feeding links are grass → grasshopper → frog → snake. After large-scale harvesting, many frogs disappear.

Which claims correctly predict effects through the ecosystem relationships? One or more options may be correct.

options.text: Grasshopper numbers may rise because fewer frogs eat them.
Snake numbers may fall because frogs, their prey, become scarce.
Only the frogs are affected; grasshoppers and snakes stay the same.
The field still looks green, so no ecosystem change has occurred.

teacher.key_rationale: Losing frogs affects prey below and predators above through the feeding links. Claiming only frogs change, or that a green look means no change, miss tracing those effects.
